classification.reason: Request is a scientific goal or asks for planning without a concrete workflow.

plan.goal: Design, rank, and explicitly submit a protein binder against the provided target sequence with the interface directed toward residues 25, 35, 36, 39, 40, 72, 73, 76, 128, and 132, returning enough ranked evidence to fill final 'Reason:' and 'Answer:' fields.
assumptions: Target hotspot residue numbers are interpreted as 1-indexed positions on the provided target sequence and mapped onto folded chain A.
The validated hotspot-directed binder workflow will be used with all 10 requested target residues as hotspot guidance.

The contact requirement is enforced as a ranking preference: candidates contacting at least 5 of the 10 requested residues are preferred when available; otherwise the best available hotspot-engaging binder is submitted.
A 60 aa binder length and multi-sample preview-scale search are acceptable defaults for an initial local reproducible design round.
Acceptable for explicit final submission means the top-ranked binder has plausible interface engagement at the requested site and no obvious QC red flags relative to the rest of the candidate set.
Provider selected a workflow template by reference; expanded it to the validated local workflow descriptor.

workflow_plan.name: target_sequence_binder_design_round
workflow_plan.description: Fold a target sequence, generate hotspot-directed binders with PXDesign pipeline mode, analyze, QC, and rank candidates.

success_criteria.final_submission: Explicitly submit the top binder with submit_candidate if acceptable after ranking.
reason_field_must_cover: why the submitted binder was selected
hotspot-contact coverage relative to the requested site
any important QC or confidence caveats
answer_field_must_cover: whether it meets the half-hotspot contact preference if available
